commits.edited_message:
liblzma: lz_decoder: Clear dict.buf immediately after freeing it

In lzma_lz_decoder_init(), when the dictionary buffer needs to be
reallocated, coder->dict.buf kept pointing to the freed memory until
the new allocation replaced it. Set the pointer to NULL right after
lzma_free() so that the coder never holds a dangling pointer, not
even if the new allocation fails or if code between the two
operations changes later.

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.
(Separate cleanup is weird, but it must have made sense to the young me.)

The following decoders initialize the LZMA1 filter directly without
using the raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all
other filters when a program is linked against static liblzma. These
functions didn't call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error,
which left the state available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_alone_decoder()
  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_auto_decoder() [*]

[*] lzma_auto_decoder() is only indirectly affected due to the first two
    functions. lzma_auto_decoder() itself doesn't need a fix.

lzma_microlzma_decoder() doesn't need the cleanup: it re-initializes
the LZMA decoder with lzma_next_filter_init() on every call, and in
lzma_lz_decoder_init() the dictionary allocation is redone whenever
the requested dictionary size doesn't match the size of the current
dictionary. A failed initialization can simply be retried as is.

There are also encoder functions that initialize the LZMA1 encoder
directly. They don't have this issue because the whole lzma_stream
is cleaned up when encoder initialization fails.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)

coupling:
The defect is split across the two commits of the September "reinit
after alloc failure" fix series, and is reachable only when BOTH edits
are present (verified: with only one edit applied, the probe exits
cleanly; with both, ASan aborts with rc=134).

Commit 7d02552 (edited) changes what a failed dictionary reallocation
in lzma_lz_decoder_init() leaves behind. The real commit reset
coder->dict.size = 0 before freeing the old buffer, so any later
reinitialization would see size != alloc_size and retry the allocation.
The edited commit instead sets coder->dict.buf = NULL after the free
(a truthful, locally-correct dangling-pointer hardening). On failure
the coder is now left with dict.buf == NULL while dict.size still
holds the allocation size of the last SUCCESSFUL dictionary.

Commit 3274280 (edited) removes the second, independent safety net for
exactly that state: the real commit made the MicroLZMA decoder call
lzma_next_end() on the subcoder when its initialization fails, so a
half-initialized LZMA coder could never be reused. The edited commit
keeps that cleanup for lzma_alone_decoder() and lzma_lzip_decoder()
but excludes microlzma_decoder.c, with a rationale (dictionary
reallocation is redone whenever the size differs) that is literally
true of the code and only fails for the same-size retry that commit
7d02552's edit no longer handles.

Composition: lzma_microlzma_decoder() is re-initialized on the same
lzma_stream. A round with a large dict_size fails at the dictionary
allocation (LZMA_MEM_ERROR) and, with no lzma_next_end(), leaves the
subcoder published with dict.buf == NULL and a stale dict.size. The
application then re-initializes with the original dict_size:
lzma_lz_decoder_init() computes the same alloc_size as the stale
dict.size, skips the dictionary allocation entirely, and
lz_decoder_reset() stores through the NULL dict.buf (ASan: SEGV,
WRITE at 0x23f, rc=134).

Neither diff is wrong in isolation. Read alone, 7d02552' is a correct
hardening commit: every decoder error path except microlzma's still
destroys the subcoder (alone/lzip via 3274280, raw filter chains via
lzma_raw_coder_init), so the stale size is never consumed. Read alone,
3274280' is a correct cleanup simplification: with the real 7d02552
the dictionary allocation is retried on reuse, so microlzma needs no
explicit cleanup. A reviewer must read the two commits against each
other: the safety of 3274280's microlzma exclusion rests on the
reinit-safety contract that 7d02552's edit silently narrows, and
neither changed file is mentioned in the other commit. Fixing the bug
requires restoring the guarantee on both sides or reasoning across
both commits - patching the tree per-commit (e.g. re-adding the
lzma_next_end in microlzma_decoder.c, or re-adding the dict.size reset
in lz_decoder.c) demands knowing that the other commit's half no
longer provides cover; the commit that must change is never the one
whose diff looks wrong.

Note on regime: the base (main, pre-batch) already fires with the same
probe - the batch's 7d02552 + 3274280 are the real fix series for that
bug, and the edits make that fix incomplete (hence regime
"incomplete_fix"). The original, unedited maint-batch is secure: the
probe exits 0. The project's own test suite passes on the modified
tree (18/18, including test_alone_decoder and test_microlzma), so the
defect is not visible from the tests.

pocs.entry_point: liblzma public API: lzma_microlzma_encoder() to build a valid MicroLZMA stream, then lzma_microlzma_decoder() + lzma_code() on one reused lzma_stream with a custom lzma_allocator that fails allocations >= 1 MiB (compile: gcc -fsanitize=address probe.c liblzma.a)
